blocks.text: The hidden cost of administrative work

Your day as an online tutor is often fragmented by small, repetitive tasks. You spend your time jumping between lesson preparation, grading, and answering emails. This constant switching makes it hard to focus on your students. Many tutors feel the burn of this hidden load. It is not just the teaching that tires you out. It is the management of the files, the scheduling, and the feedback loops. When you use AI tools for online tutoring, you can group these tasks. This keeps your focus on the lesson at hand.
Essential Mac apps for your tutoring stack

Most successful tutors on Mac do not rely on one single app. They build a stack that handles different parts of the job. You likely use GoodNotes 6 for marking up PDFs or Notability for digital handwriting. For assignments, Google Classroom acts as your central hub. If you need to create visuals, Canva is the standard. To keep your financial records and attendance in order, Numbers or Excel are the go-to tools. You might also use SupaSidebar to keep your class links and resources within reach.
How to use Lazur to save time

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you manage these apps without clicking around. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are stuck in a complex spreadsheet, ask Lazur to explain how to use a specific function. If you cannot find a button in a new app, ask Lazur to point at it. It will draw a circle and a label on your screen. When you need to write a quick email to a parent, hold fn to dictate your message. Lazur formats the text for you at the cursor.

Always follow your employer's rules regarding student data. Do not share private student information with any AI tool. Lazur does not store your screen or audio, but you are responsible for the content you process.
blocks.title: Privacy Reminder

blocks.text: When you work with student information, you must be careful. AI tools are powerful, but they are not a substitute for your judgment. Never upload sensitive documents or personal identifiers to public AI models. When using Lazur, remember that it only looks at your screen when you hold the shortcut. It does not store your history on its servers. Keep your student records in approved, encrypted platforms.

items: Use task batching to group grading, email, and planning into dedicated blocks.
Use time blocking to separate your teaching hours from your administrative hours.
Set up standard templates for progress reports to reduce manual writing.
Automate your scheduling with tools like SchedulingKit or HoneyBook.
Use AI to draft initial feedback for students before you refine it yourself.

blocks.text: Task batching is a simple way to stop the constant context switching. Instead of answering every email as it arrives, set aside 30 minutes at the start and end of your day. Use this time to handle all correspondence at once. When you prepare for your lessons, do it in a single session. This keeps your brain in a creative state for longer. If you find yourself doing the same thing every day, create a snippet in Lazur. You can dictate a full response to a common question in seconds.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not operate other apps or click buttons. It guides you, points at things, and answers questions out loud so you can do the work yourself.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe for student data?
faq.answer: Lazur does not store your screen or audio. It only processes information while you hold the shortcut key. Always follow your employer's privacy policies regarding student data.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is currently built for macOS only, supporting both Apple silicon and Intel chips.
